notes: "Here is the kind of slide this talk is about: one real result. The structure is PDB entry 1BNA, the Dickerson–Drew DNA dodecamer, drawn from its deposited coordinates; chain A is green, chain B ochre. For each of the twelve base pairs we measured the distance between the paired C1-prime atoms. The chart is not a pasted picture: it is a HUANDENG chart object holding the twelve values from the CSV, with a labelled axis that deliberately does not start at zero, so the geometric variation is visible. If a value or a label needs to change, you edit the data, not the pixels. Be careful about what the chart says: these are twelve positions in a single crystal structure. They are not replicates and carry no error bars. The shortest distance is at pair 7, a T–A pair in the central AATT region; the longest at pair 12, a terminal G–C pair.\n\nMethod: Euclidean distance between C1′ atoms, chain A residues 1–12 ascending paired with chain B residues 24–13 descending. Values from paired-c1-distances.csv, recomputed for this edition from the RCSB file by sources/independent-20261111/science/generate_1bna.py; all twelve match. Each chart category carries its position and base pair, so the labels stay aligned in PowerPoint.\n\nSource: RCSB PDB 1BNA, https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1BNA; structure DOI 10.2210/pdb1BNA/pdb. Drew HR, Wing RM, Takano T, Broka C, Tanaka S, Itakura K, Dickerson RE. PNAS 78 (1981) 2179–2183, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.78.4.2179."

designIntent.purpose: Show the twelve measured C1′–C1′ distances beside the structure they were measured in.
keep: Labelled non-zero y-axis, units in Å
No replicate, error-bar or trend claims
